title: Benji and the Mirror Light
markdown:
In Willow Creek, where the willows whispered, lived Benji, a kind lantern maker. His workshop smelled of soft paper. His hands wove lanterns that glowed like evening stars. Suki the squirrel loved to watch.

Soon: the Whispering Willow Festival, the Great Whispering Willow lit with a hundred tiny lights. Benji made a special one, the Twinkling Star, woven with moonbeam threads. He wanted the highest branch. From the ground he could not see the spot. The top hid deep in leaves.

“How can I hang it when the best place is hiding?” Suki chittered, climbed his shoulder; even then the branch stayed secret. They looked through leaves. Hard. “Perhaps another way to look.”

He remembered Dr. Farah: light is a traveler, if you know how to look. He hurried to the workshop and came back with a mirror, round and smooth as a river stone. He switched on the Twinkling Star. Warm light. Careful hands held the mirror.

He turned it just so. The lantern’s light bounced off the shiny side and painted a bright circle onto the very branch he could not see. “Look.” Suki’s eyes widened. “Two lights!” “The same light. Showing more of the world.”

He named it once: reflection. Smooth surface, bounce, new view. Suki nudged his hand. A little more left. He placed the hook, hung the lantern with a soft sigh of paper. It shimmered, a friendly greeting from the night sky.

“We did it.” He nuzzled her fur and did not wonder what other secrets light held, or think of cozy beds on the page. They sat as the moon rose, silvery on the meadow, watching the one light they had hung. The willows kept their own whispers. The hook, for once, was in the right place.
